name: Sandra Gómez
about:
I'm a multidisciplinary designer based in Barcelona, passionate about the intersection of art, technology, and human experience. I work across AI creative direction, immersive installations, interactive media, and photography — always searching for the emotional core of every project.

Currently pursuing a Master of Science in Digital Arts and Creative Technologies at La Salle Barcelona. Before that, years of hands-on work crafting campaigns, visual identities, and spatial experiences for brands and cultural projects.

I believe great design doesn't just look good — it makes people feel something.

projects.title: Studio46
projects.content:
Project Overview
Studio 46 approached me to create a series of photographs that could capture the character of the space while visitors experienced a guided tour. Located in a historic family home in Barcelona’s Gràcia neighbourhood, the studio brings together architecture, printmaking, contemporary art and decades of artistic heritage.

The images were created for the studio’s website and digital communication, with the aim of presenting not only the artworks, but also the atmosphere, history and unique details visitors encounter throughout the space.

My Approach
I followed the tour as it naturally unfolded, documenting the interaction between the visitors, the artworks and the studio itself. Rather than staging every moment, we focused on authentic reactions, movement and spontaneous details.

The photography explored the different areas of Studio 46—from its gallery rooms and original architectural features to its printing presses, tools and working spaces. The visual direction combined wider environmental shots with close-up details to communicate the studio’s intimate, lived-in character and its connection to generations of artists.

Key Deliverables
Guided-tour and visitor photography
Interior and architectural images
Artwork and exhibition details
Candid lifestyle moments
Website and digital-content photography
Visual documentation of the studio’s creative process
